paragraphs: Here's what I see in this passage, friend. Paul is standing in front of a new governor, surrounded by people bringing "many serious charges that they could not prove" (Acts 25:7). And Paul doesn't panic, doesn't beg, and doesn't make something up to smooth it over. He simply says, "I have committed no offense against the law of the Jews or against the temple or against Caesar" (Acts 25:8).

Now look at what Paul says next. "If, however, I am guilty of anything worthy of death, I do not refuse to die" (Acts 25:11). That is a man with a clear conscience, friend, and a clear conscience is a sturdy thing to stand on when everybody is pointing at you. I think the lesson is that being right doesn't mean life gets easy, but it does mean you can stand there steady while it gets hard.

Paul also uses what he has. He says, "I appeal to Caesar!" (Acts 25:11), and he does it in the open, right where he ought to be tried. Friend, you can be faithful AND wise in the same breath. The story isn't over, so keep your oven warm and see where Paul's road goes next.
